notes: Universal Crossword from Andrews McMeel's uclick data feed (code fcx), the syndicate's own XML. Named by the feed: fcxYYMMDD-data.xml. The feed carries no circles or shading.
USA Today from Andrews McMeel's uclick data feed (code usaon). Named by the feed: usaonYYMMDD-data.xml. The feed carries no circles or shading.
Universal Sunday from Andrews McMeel's uclick data feed (code usun), the syndicate's own XML. Named by the feed: usunYYMMDD-data.xml.
The daily is posted at 10 pm Eastern the evening before (6 pm on weekends). The Times rewrites clues after the day, hence the re-fetches. NYT_S, if set, is sent as the NYT-S cookie.
The Mini, posted the evening before like the daily.
The Midi, a 9x9 to 10x9 grid, posted the evening before like the daily.
The daily crossword runs Monday to Wednesday; year-end issue crosswords live under /magazine/ and are not fetched by date.
The Mini runs Thursday and Friday. The payload's date is the day it was made, not the day it ran; the file is named by the day it ran.
The Post's Sunday crossword from its games service, the JSON its player loads. The service answers an empty body for a Sunday it has no puzzle for.

The Arkadium Mini Crossword, from the feed behind Arkadium's player: Crossword Compiler XML, named by the feed (puzzle_mini_YYMMDD.xml). The feed holds a file for every date well into the next year. New puzzles ran 2018-12 to 2021 and once in 2024; every file since is a rerun of an earlier date, served under its own date. The feed's titles are the game's name or a batch number, so the title is the date.

The 2 Minute Mini, a 5x5 Arkadium publishes: the Across Lite file the feed behind its player serves, named by the feed (puzzle_YYMMDD.puz). The feed holds a file for every date well into the next year and has rerun earlier puzzles since 2024-01-30, each served under its own date. The feed's titles are numbers that don't identify a puzzle, so the title is the date. Some files have wrong .puz checksums.

The blog's crossword, posted every Monday (Themeless Monday) and Thursday. The day's post links the .puz (and a PDF, not fetched) under /files/, named by puzzle number and title (NNNNTitle.puz). The date is the post's.

The Daily Princetonian's full-size crossword, from the API behind the paper's own crossword site. It has no fixed day: about one a week in term, none over breaks and exams, so every day is asked for and most are misses. The data has no grid; it is drawn from the clues' answers and positions.
The Daily Princetonian's mini, as for dailyprincetonian.daily. It runs in bursts of a few weekdays with long gaps, so every day is asked for and most are misses.
The Los Angeles Times daily crossword, from the Amuse Labs player on the paper's games page. The puzzle id encodes the date (tcaYYMMDD), and files are named by it (tcaYYMMDD.json).

The Los Angeles Times Midi, a mid-size daily grid. Puzzle ids are the title plus the date (Title_YYYYMMDD), so the id for a date is looked up on the player's date picker, which lists only recent puzzles.
The Atlantic's daily crossword, from its Amuse Labs player. The puzzle id encodes the date (atlantic_YYYYMMDD).
Newsday's daily crossword, from its syndicate's (Creators) set on the Amuse Labs player. The puzzle id encodes the date (Creators_WEB_YYYYMMDD).
The Daily Beast's crossword, Sunday to Thursday. Puzzle ids are random hex, so the id for a date is looked up on the player's date picker, which lists about 30 recent puzzles.
The Crossword Club's daily crossword, from its Amuse Labs player. The puzzle id encodes the date (crossword-club_YYYYMMDD).
The Crossword Club's themed puzzle, on Wednesdays. Puzzle ids are random hex, looked up on the player's date picker.

Vox's crossword, Monday to Saturday. Puzzle ids are the constructor's initials plus the date and a time (XXvox_YYYYMMDD_HHMM), so the id for a date is looked up on the player's date picker. A puzzle with no title is titled by its date.

Vulture's 10x10 daily crossword, on weekdays. The date picker lists several puzzles under one date, so the id comes from the player embedded in the day's article; a day whose article isn't at its dated address is looked for at the undated one, if that page's title names the date. The payload's publish time is the evening before.
The Walrus's weekly crossword, on Fridays (a puzzle posted a day late is missed). Puzzle ids are random hex, looked up on the player's date picker.

Defector's weekly crossword, on Mondays, edited by Hoang-Kim Vu. Puzzle ids are random hex, looked up on the player's date picker. The payload names no editor, so the editor param supplies one, except on a puzzle whose byline names him. "(Themeless)" is left out of a title, and a bare year or "(c)" in the copyright line is written "© year".

Thomas Joseph, King Features' daily crossword, from GameDistribution's feed (the one behind Arkadium's and Hearst's players), which replaced King's own .jpz feed after 2025-04-18. Crossword Compiler documents as JSON, named <id>-YYYY-MM-DD.json by the feed's date. King's files name only the feature as creator, so Author is the byline, Thomas Joseph; the title is King's own, the date (October 09, 2026). Em dashes in clues are written --, en dashes -. King's data keeps hyphens that broke words for a newspaper column (Appor-tions), a few clues a year; they are kept, since telling one from a real compound (lead-in) takes a person. A space after an opening quote mark is removed; a clue with unbalanced quote marks (King's files drop closing marks and cut clues short) is listed as tricky, and so is a clue the file drops (one beginning "Down", whose number is left on the clue before), written [XXX].

Eugene Sheffer, King Features' daily crossword, from GameDistribution's feed, as for kingfeatures.thomas-joseph. Author is the byline, Eugene Sheffer. Dashes, print hyphens, quote marks and dropped clues are handled as for kingfeatures.thomas-joseph.

The Premier Crossword by Frank A. Longo (King Features), a Sunday 21x21, from GameDistribution's feed, as for kingfeatures.thomas-joseph. Author comes from King's creator line (Premier Crossword by Frank A. Longo). King's files have no puzzle title; the title is King's date (October 09, 2026). Em dashes are written --; en dashes are kept.

params: tenant=wsj offset=-1 'copyright=© The Wall Street Journal'
notes: The Wall Street Journal's crossword, Monday to Saturday, from PZLR, the platform the paper's player runs on: the embed's getLevel request answers by date with no sign-in. Files are named by the print date; PZLR dates a puzzle by its online release, the day before (offset=-1), and has it up by the morning of that day. Friday's contest puzzle is served without its answers until the contest closes on Sunday night: it is written with every white square an X until a re-fetch (through day 4) has the answers. Payloads from before PZLR's 2026 format change carry no circles or rebus squares.

The Boston Globe Magazine's Sunday crossword, by Brendan Emmett Quigley and Joon Pahk in alternate weeks, from the Globe's crossword queue on Puzzmo, where the Globe's player gets its puzzles. The queue also holds the Universal crossword Monday to Saturday, which is not fetched here (see universal.daily). Files are named by the queue's publishDate.
The Globe's daily mini, a 5x5, from the team's crossword-mini queue on Puzzmo. Puzzmo names each one by its date (Tue, Nov 3, 2026); the title is that date written out (Tuesday, November 3, 2026).

Puzzmo's own daily crossword, edited by Brian Callahan; sizes vary (11x11, 12x10). Each clue has a hint (A1 ^hint: ...) in the file as served; the .xd doesn't carry them. Fetched the way xword-dl fetches Puzzmo.

Puzzmo's own daily mini, from Puzzmo Mini Crossword #1 on 2025-10-01; not always 5x5 (9x5 on 2026-11-01). The file as served also has a Line Breaks section (where the player may wrap each clue), which the .xd doesn't need. Some days have Schrödinger squares, written as rebus squares holding both letters (1=E|K), with the clue once per reading. Fetched the way xword-dl fetches Puzzmo.

Puzzmo's Big crossword, a 15x15 played over three days from a Monday (its dailyTitle says "Nov 2-4, 2026"), filed under that Monday: every other Monday from 2025-01-13, the first Monday of each month from 2025-07-07, and every other Monday again from 2026-01-05. The other Mondays are misses. Fetched the way xword-dl fetches Puzzmo.
